text:
Heaven never
takes a day off.
why: The Image: heaven moves with inexhaustible vigor, and the realized person strengthens without ceasing. (Not a line lesson: 1-2-3 would be three line lessons in a row. The critic's 'Heaven never stops.' is 19 characters.)

text:
Frost underfoot:
ice is coming.
why: Line 1: small signs now tell you what is coming later.

text:
Without a guide,
let the deer go.
why: Line 3: chasing deer into the forest without a forester goes wrong, so let it go.

text:
Teachers don't
chase students.
why: The Judgment: it is not I who seek the youth, the youth seeks me. (Not the suggested line 2: 3, 4 and 5 would be three line lessons in a row.)

text:
Uninvited guests?
Receive them well.
why: Line 6: three uninvited guests arrive; treat them with respect and it ends well.

text:
Won the belt,
lost it by noon.
why: Line 6: a win taken by fighting is stripped away before the morning is out.

text:
Unseen water
under the earth.
why: Accepted: water within the earth is the army, the people held in reserve.

text:
Friends at lunch,
holding together.
why: Accepted: Renoir's crowded table shows holding together at a glance.

text:
Wheels come off,
the couple glares.
why: Line 3: the cart throws its spokes and husband and wife glare at each other; when something structural breaks, people on the same side turn on each other.

text:
The tiger's tail:
it does not bite.
why: Accepted: tread carefully and even the tiger does not bite.

text:
No flat ground
without a slope.
why: Line 3: no level plain without slopes. Good times tilt, and that is normal.

text:
The great leaves,
the small arrives.
why: The Judgment's own words, 'The great departs, the small arrives': the viewer can check it against the page on screen, and it says why things stall. (Judgment, not line 5, so 11-12-13 are not three line lessons in a row.)

text:
First weeping,
then laughter.
why: Line 5: fellowship can start in tears and end in laughing together.

text:
A full cart,
a place to go.
why: Line 2: a great cart for loading and somewhere to go; you have the capacity and the destination.

text:
Level the heaps,
fill the holes.
why: The Image: the mountain within the earth reduces what is excessive and increases what is lacking.

text:
Shout about it
and it goes wrong.
why: Line 1: proclaiming your enthusiasm is adverse.

text:
Grabbed the kid,
lost the adult.
why: Line 2: attached to the small child, losing the mature one. No verdict, only the trade: following one thing means letting go of another.

text:
Plan three days,
check three days.
why: The Judgment's 'three days before, three days after' gives the repair a concrete measure: think before and after.

text:
Too comfortable?
Worry a little.
why: Line 3: a comfortable approach supports nothing, but once you worry about it there is no fault.

text:
Look like a guest,
not an inspector.
why: Approved: at line 4 the supported move is to be the sovereign's guest, observing with a visitor's courtesy.

text:
Lightning shows,
thunder hits.
why: Fire over thunder: first see the problem clearly, then bite down with force.

text:
A white horse?
It's a suitor.
why: Line 4: the white horse that looks like an attacker is a suitor. Something striking arriving is not always a threat.

text:
The bed breaks at
the legs first.
why: Collapse starts at the base, the part nobody looks at.

text:
Solstice:
kings stayed home.
why: Thunder within the earth: at the solstice the ancient kings closed the passes and the ruler did not tour the regions.

text:
Innocent, yet
the ox is taken.
why: Innocence does not protect you from misfortune; it only means the misfortune is not your fault.

text:
Cap the calf's
horns early.
why: Line 4: a board on the young bull's horns, supremely good, is restraint put in place before there is harm.

text:
Stop staring at
someone's plate.
why: Line 1 sets down its own spirit tortoise to gape at someone else's meal: envy traded for self-sufficiency.

text:
In over your head.
Not your fault.
why: Line 6, over Hokusai's wave: wading too deep, the water covers the head. Adverse, but no fault.

text:
Food through
a window: no fault
why: Line 4: wine and rice handed through the window, and in the end no fault. In the abyss, a small plain offering is enough.

text:
At sunset, don't
party or wail.
why: Drumming and singing and lamenting old age are both adverse responses to the setting sun.

text:
This one ends
in a wedding.
why: The Judgment: taking a wife resolves well. The book cares whether influence becomes a commitment.

text:
No game in this
field. Move.
why: Persistence in the wrong place is wasted: a field with no game.

text:
Leaving? Take your
people with you.
why: Line 3: a tangled retreat goes well if you keep your dependents with you instead of cutting them loose.

text:
Ram hits hedge.
Horns get stuck.
why: Line 3's ram shows that force alone gets power stuck.

text:
Three audiences
in one day.
why: The Judgment shows what progress looks like when it comes: horses given in abundance and three audiences with the king in a single day.

text:
A prince acted mad
to stay alive.
why: Line 5: Prince Ji hid his sanity at the tyrant's court, the book's own example of hiding your light to survive.

text:
Whoever feeds them
holds the family.
why: Line 2: the one who stays in and feeds everyone is the center of the family, which Chardin's mother at the table shows at a glance.

text:
Not an attacker,
a suitor.
why: Line 6: what looked like a threat was someone coming to propose.

text:
Water stuck
on a mountain.
why: WATER over MOUNTAIN: water on top of a mountain can't flow and just sits there, the book's picture of obstruction.

text:
Riding with a load
invites thieves.
why: Line 3: carrying the old burden into freedom makes you a target.

text:
Two small baskets
will do.
why: The Judgment says two small baskets may be used for the offering: when you have less, a small offering is enough.

text:
Even bad events
can increase you.
why: Line 3, the surprising line of Increase: 'Increased through unfortunate events. No fault.'

text:
Tell your own
town first.
why: Before a breakthrough, the Judgment says notify your own city.

text:
A lean pig kicks.
Tie it early.
why: Line 1: the small thing that looks harmless still struggles, so restrain it at the first sign.

text:
One handshake,
laughter again.
why: Line 1: after confusion, one handclasp restores laughter, so don't worry about the arguments.

text:
A tree grows
inside the earth.
why: EARTH over WIND (wind is also wood): the Image's wood growing within the earth, pushing up through soil before anyone sees it, which answers the hook about slow growth.

text:
A lake with
no water.
why: The two trigrams, LAKE over WATER, show the water drained out below the lake: the empty lake is the book's picture of oppression.

text:
The well is clean.
No one drinks.
why: Line 3, the only sad line in the book: the well is cleaned and no one drinks, 'my heart's sorrow'.

text:
Some change only
their faces.
why: The realized person changes like a leopard; the petty change only their faces, so surface change is not the real thing.

text:
The legs break.
Duke wears dinner.
why: The caldron's legs break, the duke's meal spills over him: what happens when the setup isn't right.

text:
First fear,
then laughter.
why: The Judgment puts terror and laughter in sequence: the shock comes, then the laugh.

text:
Still inside,
while you walk.
why: The Judgment walks through the courtyard: stillness is not freezing in place, it is keeping still inside while you keep moving.

text:
Goose in a tree?
Find flat footing.
why: A goose can't grip a branch; in the wrong place it looks for a flat perch, and there is no fault.

text:
The princess wore
the plainer dress.
why: The emperor's daughter dressed plainer than her attendant, and it resolves well.

text:
Lightning to see,
thunder to act.
why: Thunder over fire: abundance gives clear sight and the force to act at the same time, and that window does not last.

text:
The wanderer burns
his own inn.
why: A guest who wrecks the shelter he was given loses his helper too.

text:
Say it too often,
it grates.
why: Line 3, repeated penetration brings friction: repeating has a limit, past which the listener pushes back.

text:
Painters toast,
then talk shop.
why: Krøyer's artists at their party: the Image joins friends for discussion and practice, not only celebration.

text:
Drop your faction,
more will gather.
why: Dissolving your own group supremely resolves well: dispersion creates accumulation, more than any faction could hold.

text:
A lake holds only
so much water.
why: Water over the lake: knowing your capacity is what keeps you from flooding.

text:
Truth even reaches
pigs and fish.
why: The Judgment opens with piglets and fish: real sincerity reaches even them.

text:
Missed the king?
See the minister.
why: Not reaching the ruler, meeting the minister: in a small time the tier below is the right channel, no fault.

text:
Fine silk turns
to rags.
why: After completion, decay is slow and quiet, so the line says to stay watchful all day.

text:
Almost across,
the fox gets wet.
why: The little fox has almost crossed and wets its tail: the last step is where it goes wrong.
